entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Neroccio di Bartolomeo de' Landi (1447–1500) was a renowned Italian painter and sculptor of the early-Renaissance or Quattrocento period in Siena, Italy.

As a leading artist of his time, he was deeply influenced by the works of the ancient Greeks and Romans, which he studied in Florence and later in Rome.

His most notable works include the 'Madonna and Child with Saint John the Baptist' and the 'St. Sebastian', both of which showcase his mastery of humanism and classical themes.

De' Landi's contributions to the development of Renaissance art were significant, as he helped to establish Siena as a major artistic center, and his works paved the way for future generations of artists.

In his later years, de' Landi became increasingly fascinated with the mystical and spiritual aspects of art, which led him to create works that blended realistic depictions with symbolic and allegorical elements.

The legacy of Neroccio di Bartolomeo de' Landi can be seen in the works of later artists, such as Sandro Botticelli and Domenico Ghirlandaio, who were heavily influenced by his style and techniques.

As a testament to his enduring influence, de' Landi's works continue to be celebrated and studied by art historians and enthusiasts around the world.

In 2010, de' Landi's 'Madonna and Child with Saint John the Baptist' was purchased by the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York for $35 million, solidifying his status as one of the most important artists of the Renaissance.

This acquisition marked a turning point in the recognition of de' Landi's contributions to the development of Western art, and it serves as a reminder of the enduring power of his art to inspire and educate future generations.

As a key figure in the Quattrocento movement, de' Landi's impact on the course of art history is undeniable, and his works continue to be celebrated for their beauty, craftsmanship, and historical significance.
